title: Graph Explorer
intro: A graph is a set of vertices connected by edges. Build a graph — at random or by hand — then choose an algorithm and follow, step by step, how it works on your graph.

bfs.name: Breadth-First Search (BFS)
bfs.summary: Explores the graph in layers: first the vertices one edge away from the start, then those two edges away, and so on. It uses a queue.

dfs.name: Depth-First Search (DFS)
dfs.summary: Follows a path as deep as possible, then backtracks to the most recent vertex that still has unexamined neighbours. It uses a stack.

components.name: Connected components
components.summary: Runs a breadth-first search from every vertex not reached yet, which splits the graph into its connected components and numbers them.

dijkstra.name: Dijkstra
dijkstra.summary: Shortest paths from one start vertex when no weight is negative. It settles the nearest unsettled vertex over and over.

bellmanFord.name: Bellman–Ford
bellmanFord.summary: Shortest paths from one start vertex that also work with negative weights, and that report a negative cycle when one is reachable.

floydWarshall.name: Floyd–Warshall
floydWarshall.summary: Shortest paths between every pair of vertices, built in a matrix one pivot vertex at a time.

kruskal.name: Kruskal
kruskal.summary: A minimum spanning tree built by taking the lightest edges first and skipping those that would close a cycle. It uses union–find.

prim.name: Prim
prim.summary: A minimum spanning tree grown from one start vertex, always adding the cheapest edge that leaves the tree.

kahn.name: Kahn (topological sort)
kahn.summary: Orders the vertices of a directed graph so that every arc points forward, and detects a cycle when no such order exists.

unmet.nonEmpty: The graph has no vertices yet: add one or generate a graph.
unmet.directed: This algorithm needs a directed graph: an arc has to point somewhere for the question to make sense.
unmet.undirected: This algorithm needs an undirected graph: the structure it builds has no direction.
unmet.weighted: This algorithm compares weights, so it needs a weighted graph.
unmet.nonNegativeWeights: Dijkstra settles a vertex for good, which a negative weight can contradict. Use Bellman–Ford for negative weights.

panel.queueHint: Front of the queue on the left.

notice.negativeCycle: The arc {{from}} → {{to}} can still be relaxed after n − 1 passes: a cycle of negative total weight is reachable, so no shortest distance exists.
notice.negativeCycleVertices: These vertices lie on a cycle of negative total weight: {{vertices}}. Distances through them are meaningless.
notice.spanningForest: The graph is split into {{trees}} components, so the result is a minimum spanning forest: one tree per component, not a spanning tree.
notice.primPartial: Prim grows a single tree, so it reached only {{reached}} of {{total}} vertices: the rest are in other components.
notice.cycle: These vertices form or follow a cycle, so no topological order exists: {{vertices}}.

traversal.dequeue: Take {{vertex}} out of the queue and examine its neighbours.
traversal.discover: {{from}} reaches {{vertex}}: discover it and add it to the frontier.
traversal.skipNeighbor: {{vertex}} had already been reached, so the edge from {{from}} adds nothing.
traversal.finish: Every neighbour of {{vertex}} has been examined: it is finished.
traversal.complete: Traversal complete: every vertex reachable from the start was visited.
traversal.completeWithUnreached: Traversal complete. These vertices were never reached, because they lie outside the start vertex’s component: {{vertices}}.

components.restart: No component holds {{vertex}} yet, so it starts component {{component}}.
components.dequeue: Take {{vertex}} out of the queue: it belongs to component {{component}}.
components.discover: {{from}} reaches {{vertex}}, so {{vertex}} belongs to component {{component}} too.
components.skipNeighbor: {{vertex}} is already in a component, so the edge from {{from}} adds nothing.
components.empty: The graph has no vertices, so it has no components.
components.complete_one: Finished: the whole graph is one connected component.
components.complete_other: Finished: the graph has {{count}} connected components.

dijkstra.start: The distance to {{vertex}} is 0 and every other distance is still unknown (∞).
dijkstra.select: {{vertex}} has the smallest distance among the vertices not settled yet ({{distance}}), so its distance is final.
dijkstra.relax: The path through {{from}} reaches {{to}} with {{distance}} ({{weight}} on this arc): that is better, so the distance drops.
dijkstra.noChange: Through {{from}}, {{to}} would cost {{candidate}}, which is no better than {{current}}: nothing changes.
dijkstra.complete: Finished: every vertex has its shortest distance from the start.
dijkstra.completeWithUnreached: Finished. These vertices stay at ∞, because no path leads to them from the start vertex: {{vertices}}.

bellman.start: The distance to {{vertex}} is 0 and every other distance is ∞. Up to {{passes}} passes over all arcs follow.
bellman.pass: Pass {{pass}} of {{total}}: relax every arc once, in order.
bellman.relax: {{from}} → {{to}} ({{weight}}) gives {{distance}}, which is better: the distance drops.
bellman.noChange: {{from}} → {{to}} ({{weight}}) would give {{candidate}}, which is no better than {{current}}: nothing changes.
bellman.skipUnreached: {{from}} has no distance yet, so the arc to {{to}} cannot be used.
bellman.settledEarly: Pass {{pass}} changed nothing, so no later pass can either: the distances are final.
bellman.negativeCycle: {{from}} → {{to}} can still be relaxed: a cycle of negative total weight is reachable and the distances are void.
bellman.complete: Finished after {{passes}} passes: every distance is final.
bellman.completeWithUnreached: Finished after {{passes}} passes. These vertices stay at ∞, because no path leads to them: {{vertices}}.

floyd.start: The matrix starts with the arc weights, 0 on the diagonal and ∞ where there is no arc. Every vertex then serves as a pivot in turn.
floyd.pivot: Pivot {{vertex}}: may a detour through {{vertex}} shorten any path?
floyd.row: Row {{from}}: compare each distance from {{from}} against going through {{pivot}}.
floyd.improve: {{from}} → {{to}} through {{pivot}} costs {{after}}, less than {{before}}: the cell drops.
floyd.complete: Finished: the matrix holds the shortest distance between every pair of vertices.
floyd.completeNegativeCycle: Finished, but these vertices ended with a negative value on the diagonal, so they lie on a cycle of negative total weight: {{vertices}}.

kruskal.start: Every vertex is its own component. The edges are examined from the lightest to the heaviest ({{edges}} in total).
kruskal.consider: Edge {{from}} – {{to}} with weight {{weight}}: are its ends in different components?
kruskal.accept: Yes, so {{from}} – {{to}} joins the tree. Edges in the tree: {{edges}}. Total weight: {{total}}.
kruskal.reject: No: {{from}} and {{to}} are already in the same component, so this edge would close a cycle. Skip it.
kruskal.complete: Finished: a minimum spanning tree. Edges: {{edges}}. Total weight: {{total}}.
kruskal.completeForest: Finished: one tree per component, {{trees}} in all. Edges: {{edges}}. Total weight: {{total}}.

prim.startVertex: {{vertex}} is the first vertex of the tree.
prim.accept: {{vertex}} joins the tree over its cheapest edge ({{weight}}): total weight {{total}}.
prim.insideTree: {{to}} is already in the tree, so the edge from {{from}} would close a cycle.
prim.improveFringe: {{vertex}} can now be reached from {{from}} for {{weight}}, cheaper than {{previous}}.
prim.keepFringe: Reaching {{vertex}} this way costs {{weight}}, which is no better than {{current}}.
prim.complete: Finished: a minimum spanning tree. Edges: {{edges}}. Total weight: {{total}}.
prim.completePartial: Finished: edges {{edges}}, total weight {{total}}, {{reached}} vertices reached. Prim grows a single tree, so these stayed out of reach: {{vertices}}.

kahn.start: These vertices have no incoming arc, so nothing has to come before them: they are ready. {{vertices}}.
kahn.emit: {{vertex}} is ready: it takes position {{position}} in the order. Its outgoing arcs are now removed.
kahn.ready: {{from}} was the last arc into {{vertex}}, so {{vertex}} is ready.
kahn.decrement: {{vertex}} still waits for {{inDegree}} arcs after the one from {{from}}.
kahn.cycle: The ready queue is empty but these vertices are left: {{vertices}}. Each still has an incoming arc, so they contain a cycle and no topological order exists.
kahn.complete: Finished: {{order}} is a valid topological order.
kahn.startNoneReady: Every vertex has an incoming arc, so nothing is ready to start.
